Transmission line fault.provides: instant loss of one path, power redistributing to parallel lines

Generator trip.requires: loss of a synchronised generating unit
Generator trip.provides: instant loss of supply, frequency deviation, no change to network topology

Substation cyber intrusion.provides: adversarial simultaneous switching, false telemetry, no physical damage

Extreme demand peak.provides: slow build over hours, forecastable, no equipment failure

Geomagnetic storm.provides: hours of warning, transformer saturation, wide simultaneous geographic effect

Overload on remaining lines.requires: a topology change that redistributes flow
Overload on remaining lines.provides: sequential trips over seconds to minutes

Frequency collapse.provides: system-wide effect within seconds, no dependence on topology

Protection system mis-operation.requires: relays acting on incorrect or adversarial inputs
Protection system mis-operation.provides: trips of healthy equipment, no underlying physical fault

Automatic load shedding.requires: pre-armed relays and a measurable frequency or voltage trigger
Automatic load shedding.provides: response within cycles, blunt and indiscriminate

Islanding into sub-grids.requires: pre-planned separation points and local generation
Islanding into sub-grids.provides: preservation of parts of the system, seconds to act

Manual dispatch reconfiguration.requires: operators with a valid system picture and minutes to act
Manual dispatch reconfiguration.provides: targeted correction, useless against sub-second events

Black start from reserve.provides: restoration from nothing, hours to days

Hours.requires: partial collapse with generation still synchronised somewhere

Days.requires: physical equipment damage or total collapse

_v1_notes.INITIATING EVENT|PROPAGATION MECHANISM: frequency collapse requires a generation-demand imbalance, so only a generator trip produces it directly - a line fault, a cyber intrusion, a demand peak and a storm all act through topology or equipment, not through instantaneous imbalance. Protection mis-operation requires incorrect inputs, which a cyber intrusion and a geomagnetic storm supply but a simple line fault, generator trip or demand peak do not. Voltage collapse needs reactive shortfall, absent in a cyber intrusion with no physical damage.
_v1_notes.INITIATING EVENT|CONTAINMENT: black start requires total collapse, which a line fault, a generator trip and a demand peak do not produce on their own. Automatic load shedding is N against a cyber intrusion because the intrusion supplies false telemetry, which is exactly what defeats a trigger-based scheme. Islanding is N against a demand peak: separation does not create generation.
_v1_notes.INITIATING EVENT|RESTORATION TIME: days requires physical damage, so a line fault, a generator trip and a demand peak are N. Cyber intrusion and geomagnetic storm are N at minutes: the first requires forensic confidence before reconnecting, the second saturates transformers.
_v1_notes.PROPAGATION MECHANISM|CONTAINMENT: overload cascades are sequential, not triggered by frequency or voltage thresholds, so automatic shedding is N. Voltage collapse is localised and progressive, so islanding is N and black start is N. Protection mis-operation defeats automatic shedding (same faulty inputs) and manual reconfiguration (the operator's picture is wrong).
_v1_notes.PROPAGATION MECHANISM|RESTORATION TIME: only frequency collapse routinely leaves damaged plant behind, so days is Y there and N for the others.
_v1_notes.CONTAINMENT|RESTORATION TIME: black start takes hours to days by definition, so minutes and hours are N. Everything else is N at days, since a containment measure that worked does not leave a multi-day outage.
